source: operator-confirmed table, superseding the handwritten note in capture_20260830_234933_photo
revision_history: v1 2026-08-30: 5.5 x 3.75 x 3.5 m estimate. Superseded — 24 cm out on ceiling, ~45 cm out on wall length, and rectangular-only.
v2 2026-08-30: per-wall, heights 325.4/325.9 varying by 0.5 cm, window height 110.5. Superseded.
v3 2026-08-31: heights corrected to a uniform 329.4 (+3.75 cm on v2), window height 110.9. Wall lengths and floor unchanged.

v4 2026-08-31: second door added on wall C (1.850 x 0.855 m, identical to the wall D door). The 40 cm floor-versus-wall gap is resolved: it is two 20 cm door reveals, i.e. the wall thickness visible inside each door opening. 497.7 - 2x20 = 457.7 exactly.
units_note: Source values are centimetres, recorded here in metres.
ceiling_note: All four corners now measure identically, so the ground truth asserts a flat ceiling and the full 1.5 cm gate is available to the pipeline. This replaces v2, which showed a 0.5 cm corner-to-corner spread; that spread was an artefact of the superseded numbers, not a property of the room.
shape_note: Walls A and C differ by 8.0 cm (1.6%) while B and D agree exactly. The room is genuinely not square, which is why per-wall ground truth is required.
open_questions: Both doors are said to account for the 40 cm, but only wall C reconciles arithmetically (497.7 - 40 = 457.7, whereas 505.7 - 40 = 465.7). Are both door reveals on wall C, or is the wall D door's reveal reducing the short floor dimension instead? This changes which wall the scorer applies the correction to.
Direct tape reading across one door reveal, to confirm the 20 cm wall thickness that is currently derived rather than measured.
Is A-B-C-D clockwise or anticlockwise, and which door is the entry?
Tape uncertainty: re-measure one wall and one opening three times to get a spread.
method_note: Tape. Uncertainty is not yet quantified: a single-pass tape run over a ~5 m wall carries sag, corner placement and reading error, and the opening gate is 2 cm. Cheapest way to pin it is to re-measure one wall and one opening three times and take the spread — until then we cannot honestly quote a ground-truth interval, and any pipeline error smaller than that spread is unmeasurable.
openings_note: Three openings: a window and a door on wall C, a door on wall D. Both doors are 1.850 x 0.855 m. Opening detection is scored with a missed opening and a phantom opening each counting as a miss, so the count itself is part of the answer key: finding two of these three costs one miss, and inventing a fourth costs another.
wall_thickness_note: Derived, not directly measured: the 40 cm floor-versus-wall gap divided by two door reveals. A 20 cm wall is thick, consistent with masonry construction and with the 3.294 m ceiling. Worth confirming with a direct tape reading across one door reveal, since it now carries weight in the scoring.

floor_vs_wall.cause: Two door reveals of 0.20 m each. 497.7 - 2 x 20 = 457.7 cm exactly.
floor_vs_wall.scoring_consequence: Wall length and clear floor are different quantities and the scorer must not compare them. A reconstruction sees the room-side wall surface, so it should recover 4.977 m for wall C; comparing that against the 4.577 m floor figure would report an 8% error that is really two doorways. Floor area must likewise be computed from wall lengths, not from the tape's floor run.
floor_vs_wall.arithmetic_note: The 40 cm reconciles against wall C (4.977 m) and not against wall A (5.057 m), which is consistent with the long floor run having been measured along the C direction.
